title: Clamp a part to the mill table with a strap clamp, its heel on the step-block tread that levels it
instruction: Clamp the blue part to the mill table with the red strap clamp.
context: Machinists and mill setup operators hold work with strap clamps: the heel rests on a step-block tread level with or just above the part, the stud sits nearer the part, and the nut goes down last (O*NET 51-4041.00 Machinists; 51-4035.00 Milling and Planing Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders). Board clamp tasks use vises, cams and bar clamps; none builds a level strap clamp from loose parts. This one adds choosing and placing the tread, threading a slotted strap onto a stud under a raised nut, then running the nut down.
setup: Positions are object centres in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left (negative toward the right arm). Table: oak top, arm bases 61 cm apart on its near edge. Mill table plate: dark grey steel, 22 x 16 x 1 cm, x 16 to 38, y -10 to 6, fixed. On it: blue steel part, 6 x 6 x 4 cm, 350 g, centre x 20.2, y -2, against two fixed grey steel stops 1 cm thick and 2.5 cm tall, one on its -x face (x 16.2 to 17.2) and one on its -y face (y -6 to -5). Grey steel stud, 1.2 cm across, rising to 13 cm above the table, at x 27, y -2. Orange steel nut, 3 x 3 x 1.2 cm with a 1.6 cm hole, on the stud, raised with its underside 11 cm above the table; it slides down the stud to 5.2 cm above the table and stays where it is put. Its yellow handle, 1.8 x 1.8 x 3 cm, sits on a 1.5 cm arm off the nut's -y face (centre x 27, y -5.9). Overhead mill arm: grey steel bar 11 x 2 x 1.5 cm, 20 to 21.5 cm above the table, x 10 to 21, y -3 to -1, on a grey column 3 x 3 x 21.5 cm at x 11.5, y -2; it holds a black end mill, 1.6 cm across and 8 cm long, at x 20, y -2, its tip 12 cm above the table. Red steel strap: bar 11.5 x 4.2 x 1.2 cm, 60 g, with a slot 1.8 cm wide and 7 cm deep open at one end, and a white grip tab 1.8 x 3 x 3 cm on top, 1 cm from the closed end; centre x 30, y -17, long side along x, slot end toward the arms. Yellow aluminium step block: 8 x 4 cm, 80 g, four 2 cm treads 2, 3, 4 and 5 cm tall (measured from its underside) rising in +x; centre x 24, y 15, long side along x.
scoring: Open both grippers, then measure with a top photo and a ruler. Score 0 if the part ever moved more than 3 mm from its start, or the strap is off the table or held up (underside over 1 cm above every support). Otherwise 1.0 if the strap is level and the nut is down; 0.5 if level with the nut up; 0.25 if the strap's toe rests on the part and its heel on any tread, tilted at most 8 degrees; else 0. Level: stud inside the slot; toe on the part (toe underside within 2 mm of the part's top, 1.0 to 2.5 cm of toe over its edge); heel end resting on a tread; heel end 0 to 4 mm higher than the toe end (about 0 to 2 degrees); strap tilted at most 3 degrees. Nut down: its underside within 3 mm of the strap's top. A nut run down first blocks the slot. Pushing cannot score: the strap must be lifted onto supports 4 cm up. Full score needs everything still. Ruler: toe and heel heights.
reset_notes: Put the part against both stops, the strap and step block at their start spots, and the nut back at the top of the stud (it stays where it is put).
fidelity: Approximate. The nut is a sliding ring on the stud with no thread: heavy damping holds it where it is put (it creeps down about 0.05 mm/s). No clamping force or torque. Rigid parts, friction 0.8. The simulator scores the last step without opening the grippers, so a strap or block still held in the air (bottom more than 1 cm above every support) counts as not placed; no area is forbidden.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (right arm reached over the plate, strap and step block never moved); demo: 1.0 (left arm set step block by the part, right arm laid strap on, both retreated)
